facts.text: Net leverage on reported EBITDA rose from 0.56x at the end of 2024 to 4.89x at the end of 2025, peaked at 5.14x at 2026-03-31 and was 3.21x at 2026-09-30. Both moves came mainly from the earnings denominator: reported EBITDA fell from USD 401,724 thousand in 2024 to USD 124,570 thousand in 2025 as other income dropped and operating income turned negative, and it rebuilt to USD 439,050 thousand over the last twelve months as weak 2025 quarters rolled off and 2026 other income came in, while net debt rose from USD 609.575 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 1,409.220 million at 2026-09-30. For creditors the ratio is a poor guide to debt-service capacity because it moves with investment marks and equity compensation more than with operating cash. facts.text: Other income, net of 250,789 thousand over the last twelve months equals 57.12% of reported EBITDA, and EBITDA before other income is 188,261 thousand, which puts net debt at 7.49x that measure. Most of the other income is mark-to-market and realised gains on strategic investments, which the filings describe as driven by observable price changes at one investee, so it can reverse and it is not cash available to service debt. The risk mechanism is that a fall in the investee's valuation would lower reported EBITDA and lift reported leverage without any change in operations. Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: no source states the legal rank or security of the 2030, 2031 and 2033 notes, so the debt stack is not drawn and note ranking is not established; the action is to obtain the indentures. - Medium: the debt note prints only a total carrying amount, so the carrying value of each note is not stated and the principal of each note stands in the instrument table beside one financing cost adjustment row. - Medium: the quarterly reports state compliance with the revolver covenants but print no ratio, and the covenant levels after the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so covenant headroom is not established; the action is to obtain the compliance certificates. - Medium: reported EBITDA includes other income, net, mostly gains on strategic investments, and adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026 without recasting 2025, so leverage and cover are shown on both measures and neither is clean; the action is to restate the 2025 periods on the 2026 definition. - Medium: the cash share of the Skydio tender offer and secondary purchases and the date of each closing are not established, so the pro forma net debt for those purchases is not stated. - Low: cash flow lines that the filings print as a dash are marked Not supplied rather than zero, and lines that a filing does not print at all are marked Not supplied; these cells are in the cash flow table and affect no printed subtotal. - Low: annual recurring revenue is not stated in the quarterly reports, so the series stops at the 2025 year end; the action is to read the issuer's investor materials. - Low: the remaining performance obligations of the original 2024 report may carry the immaterial errors the 2025 annual report describes; the value is shown as printed. - Low: the 2027 convertible notes were classified as long-term in the original 2024 report and as current in the 2025 annual report; the 2025 annual report is used for 2024 balances and the carrying amount is unchanged. - Low: the segment realignment means segment figures before 2024 are not on the current basis. - Low: the Q3 2026 report is unaudited and the period from 2026-11-05 to the as-of date is not covered by any supplied document.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Recurring software is now the larger and faster-growing half of the business, which gives creditors contracted visibility but ties it to public budgets. Software and Services made up 45.39% of net sales in the nine months of 2026 against 43.38% a year earlier and grew 38.28%, while Connected Devices grew 27.46%. Remaining performance obligations were USD 10.2 billion at 2026-09-30, and Axon expects 20% to 25% of that within 12 months, so most of the contracted value is realised over several years and depends on agency appropriations. Sales are concentrated by geography, with 82.47% in the United States, and the largest customer vertical is law enforcement, although no customer exceeded 10% of net sales in 2025, 2024 or 2023. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Payout policy is creditor-friendly on the evidence, but equity pay is settled partly in cash. Axon has declared no dividends and says it does not intend to, and it repurchased no shares under its authorised program in 2023, 2024 or 2025, leaving USD 16.3 million of the authorisation unused. Instead, net-settling employee equity awards took cash payments of USD 350,981 thousand in 2025 and USD 167,156 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, equal to 55.34% and 38.42% of stock-based compensation expense, while an at-the-market equity program raised USD 489,554 thousand in 2025 and USD 100,259 thousand in 2026 to date, which adds to equity and not to debt. Shares outstanding rose 6.25% between 2024-12-31 and 2026-09-30. facts.text: Acquisitions follow a consistent pattern of building a minority stake and then buying the rest with cash, which concentrates integration and goodwill risk. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Creditor protection rests on filing summaries and on a structure with no subsidiary guarantees. The notes and the revolver are the parent's obligations, none of its subsidiaries guarantees the senior or convertible notes, and the non-guarantor subsidiaries produced 19% of nine-month net sales and held 17% of consolidated assets. The revolver is senior unsecured at USD 500.0 million after the September 2026 amendment, undrawn, with letters of credit of USD 9.1 million, and a change of control would oblige Axon to offer to repurchase the senior notes at 101%. The covenant levels after the amendment and every restricted-payment, investment and lien basket are not printed, so what the documents allow cannot be set against what Axon has done. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The reporting record is the weakest governance evidence, although it is improving. Management reported a material weakness in revenue-recognition controls at both 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31, an amended 2024 annual report restated the classification of the 2027 convertible notes, and earlier statements were revised for principal-versus-agent accounting; the weakness was reported remediated at 2026-06-30 and disclosure controls were effective at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is that Axon behaves conservatively where creditors are most exposed: it pays no dividends, funds acquisitions from cash on hand, reports USD 1,640,404 thousand of cash and short-term investments at 2026-09-30 against USD 2,900,000 thousand of notes, and has USD 10.2 billion of contracted obligations behind its software revenue, and its revenue-recognition control weakness has been reported remediated. The view would move toward low governance risk if a proxy statement showed an independent board, no related-party dealings and a dispersed share register, and if the indentures showed tight limits on payments and investments. It would move the other way if the Skydio closings use cash near the USD 720.0 million ceiling and a stake of about 37% is followed by an agreement to take control, if the strategic investment gains reverse, if another control weakness is reported, or if acquisitions start to be funded with debt. facts.label: T2D.9 Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by a two-year control weakness record and an acquisitive, investment-heavy capital allocation, because they weaken the reliability of reported figures and convert cash into goodwill and minority stakes, which implies lower comfort in historical covenant figures and a growing cash call from Skydio. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends and repurchases, cash funding of acquisitions and disclosure controls reported effective at the last two quarter ends. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the executed debt documents. Completed with limitations; key gaps are board independence, holder percentages, related-party dealings and restricted-payment capacity.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a stronger credit is that Axon holds more liquidity than its leverage ratios suggest, pays no distributions, and is covered 8.13x on issuer-adjusted cash interest with net leverage of 1.59x on that measure (the pro forma figure is not established). On that reading the thin free cash flow is a choice to fund growth and equity pay, and the gains in other income are a bonus and not a support. That view would win if the investment gains proved recurring or realised in cash, if free cash flow after equity-pay taxes turned positive without new equity, and if the executed debt documents showed tight limits on payments and investments. The view would weaken if the Skydio cash settlement approached the USD 720.0 million ceiling while operating cash flow stayed weak, if the investment gains reversed, if the equity offering program were no longer available, or if the share price reached the level at which holders may convert the 2031 notes and Axon chose cash settlement. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation I6; calculation I8

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Axon is a listed company with no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder, so creditors cannot assume sponsor support or sponsor extraction. Business & governance found no dividends or program repurchases, eight directors who signed the 2025 annual report against ten a year earlier, a chief executive who is also a director and the officer who reviews segment results, and no holder percentages, because the proxy statement is not supplied. Group structure is simple for creditors: the notes and revolver are the parent's obligations, no subsidiary guarantees the notes, and non-guarantor subsidiaries produced 19% of nine-month net sales and held 17% of consolidated assets, so the notes have no direct claim on those entities. facts.label: Porter's Five Forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high and fragmented: the annual report lists dozens of competitors across body cameras, evidence software, records, real-time operations and counter-drone systems, including Motorola Solutions, so price and feature competition can compress margins. The threat of new entrants is moderate, because agencies require integration with evidence workflows and the TASER 10 device needs a federal firearms license, but the records software area is fragmented with more than 50 providers. The threat of substitutes is moderate, because less-lethal alternatives such as pepper spray and rubber rounds compete with conducted energy devices. Buyer power is meaningful, because buyers are public agencies with open bidding and appropriation cycles, though none exceeds 10% of sales. Supplier power is moderate to high for the TASER 10 device, because a limited number of suppliers provide its raw materials and Axon states it cannot change suppliers easily, and memory costs rose. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months, tailwinds are backlog conversion (the 20% to 25% expected within 12 months), software adoption and positive operating leverage, and headwinds are the Skydio cash settlement, memory costs, counter-drone timing and tariffs. The effect is to support revenue and interest cover while pressuring liquidity and free cash flow after equity-award taxes. Over three to five years, the 2030 senior notes and the 2031 convertible notes come due or can be put within 12 months of each other, so deleveraging depends on cash flow improving or on equity funding continuing; the sector tailwind is demand for public-safety technology, and the headwind is budget dependence and competition. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Axon presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring software contracts, large liquidity and payout discipline, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow after equity-award taxes, investment-dependent earnings and growing acquisition and investment cash calls. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate, because EBITDA converts poorly to free cash flow and the equity programs fill the gap. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access and liquidity in 2029 and 2030, because USD 2,150,000 thousand falls due or can be put within 12 months. The primary downside path is a reversal of investment gains with stalled free cash flow, and further analysis would require ratings, covenant levels after the amendment, guidance, the proxy statement and the executed debt documents. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C2

# Source readiness: Axon Enterprise, Inc.
## Request

Source readiness for Axon Enterprise, Inc. (issuer axon-1069183), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied filings can support the financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work requested for this run. No credit conclusion is drawn here.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings support a credit snapshot of Axon built from its own statements to 2026-09-30, but not covenant, governance or market-based conclusions, because executed debt documents, a proxy statement, ratings and market data are absent. Creditors should treat leverage, liquidity and debt terms as filing-level evidence only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2

Two source conflicts need care. The original 2024 annual report was later amended and its 2024 debt classification restated, so the 2025 annual report controls those comparatives. A material weakness in revenue-recognition controls was reported at 2025-12-31 and described as remediated by 2026-06-30.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_axon_axon-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–148; 10-Q_2026-06-30_axon_axon-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

The newest report, signed 2026-11-05, describes a September 2026 convertible issue and a November 2026 commitment of up to USD 1.2 billion for equity investments in Skydio after the quarter end, so period figures and later events must stay separate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

# Financial foundation: Axon Enterprise, Inc.
## Request

Financial foundation for Axon Enterprise, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway, built from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, last-twelve-month metrics and definition conflicts, with no credit recommendation.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Axon's reported net leverage of 3.21x at 2026-09-30 rests on investment gains: net debt of USD 1,409.22 million against last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of USD 439.05 million, of which 57.12% is other income, so creditors should read leverage and cover on operating earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C5; calculation C18; calculation C55

The September 2026 issue of USD 1,150 million of zero-coupon convertible notes raised debt and cash together and adds no cash coupon, so cash interest cover of 4.03x reflects only the two senior note series, and the Skydio commitment of up to USD 720.0 million in cash after the quarter end is not in these figures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C47; calculation C66

On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, net leverage is 1.59x, but the adjusted figures for 2025 and 2026 follow different definitions, so the two measures bracket the position rather than settle it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46; calculation C49
### Evidence, risk and credit analysis

Net leverage on reported EBITDA rose from 0.56x at the end of 2024 to 4.89x at the end of 2025, peaked at 5.14x at 2026-03-31 and was 3.21x at 2026-09-30. Both moves came mainly from the earnings denominator: reported EBITDA fell from USD 401,724 thousand in 2024 to USD 124,570 thousand in 2025 as other income dropped and operating income turned negative, and it rebuilt to USD 439,050 thousand over the last twelve months as weak 2025 quarters rolled off and 2026 other income came in, while net debt rose from USD 609.575 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 1,409.220 million at 2026-09-30. For creditors the ratio is a poor guide to debt-service capacity because it moves with investment marks and equity compensation more than with operating cash.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 85–87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C22; calculation C28; calculation C34; calculation C40; calculation C46

Other income, net of 250,789 thousand over the last twelve months equals 57.12% of reported EBITDA, and EBITDA before other income is 188,261 thousand, which puts net debt at 7.49x that measure. Most of the other income is mark-to-market and realised gains on strategic investments, which the filings describe as driven by observable price changes at one investee, so it can reverse and it is not cash available to service debt. The risk mechanism is that a fall in the investee's valuation would lower reported EBITDA and lift reported leverage without any change in operations.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C53; calculation C54; calculation C55; calculation C56

Cash interest paid over the last twelve months was USD 108,892 thousand against an annual cash coupon of USD 108.125 million on the 2030 and 2033 notes, so cover of 4.03x on reported EBITDA and 8.13x on adjusted EBITDA is adequate today. The 2031 convertible notes carry a zero coupon, so the September 2026 issue adds no recurring cash interest, but the capped call that cost USD 114.885 million and a conversion that may be settled in cash or shares create a future cash or dilution call that interest cover does not show.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C20; calculation C62; calculation C47; calculation C50

Operating cash flow was weak against profit. Net cash from operating activities was 225,482 thousand over the last twelve months and purchases of property and equipment were 144,570 thousand, so free cash flow was 80,912 thousand, while net income for nine months 2026 of 255,745 thousand included 257,616 thousand of non-cash gains on strategic investments. Receivables and contract assets rose 448,926 thousand and inventory rose 238,141 thousand in the nine months, partly offset by deferred revenue of 85,227 thousand, as the issuer bought materials ahead for TASER 10 and counter-drone equipment, so growth consumes cash before it converts. Free cash flow after cash interest is therefore small against the debt and against the cash the issuer has committed to Skydio, so acquisitions and investments are funded from the balance sheet and not from operations.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; calculation C57; calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C20

Scale is growing but operating profit is thin. Net sales were 3,417,012 thousand over the last twelve months against 2,779,536 thousand in 2025, yet income from operations was only 67,983 thousand because selling, general and administrative plus research and development expenses took 52.05% of third-quarter sales and gross margin fell to 56.68% in the quarter on a larger mix of counter-drone equipment and higher memory costs. The creditor consequence is that debt service depends on sustaining growth in subscription revenue and on cash from the balance sheet, and not yet on operating margin.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C51; calculation C17; calculation C60; calculation C61

Liquidity is strong against the debt. Cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, marketable securities and the undrawn revolver together came to USD 2,146.055 million at 2026-09-30, and no note matures before March 2030. The 2031 convertible notes can become convertible at the holders' option from the first quarter of 2027 only if the share price stays at least 130% of the conversion price for 20 of 30 trading days, and the issuer may settle in cash, shares or a mix, so near-term cash calls from conversion are possible but within the issuer's choice. The Skydio agreements of 2026-11-05 allow cash of up to USD 720.0 million, of which USD 127.5 million was paid on the closing date, so a further amount of up to USD 592.5 million can leave in the next two quarters; the issuer states that the remaining cash will come from cash on hand, so the cash raised in September is largely committed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C63; calculation C64; calculation C65; calculation C66

Deferred revenue is a non-debt funding float: total deferred revenue was 1,177,573 thousand at 2026-09-30 against 1,074,610 thousand at 2025-12-31, and customer deposits were 17,020 thousand. It funds operations without interest and unwinds only as service is delivered, so a slowdown in subscription billings would shrink cash inflows before it shows in revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C68; calculation C69

The strongest contrary evidence is that adjusted leverage is low and liquidity is large: net debt is 1.59x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and total liquidity of USD 2,146.055 million exceeds pro forma net debt of USD 1,536.720 million after the first Skydio payment. That view wins if the other income proves recurring and stock-based compensation is accepted as a non-cash cost; it loses if the strategic-investment marks reverse or if equity compensation has to be settled in cash, as the tax payments for net-settled awards of USD 167.156 million in nine months 2026 already show.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C49; calculation C63; calculation C64

Two data-quality limits bear on every figure above. The 2025 annual report reported a material weakness in revenue-recognition controls with immaterial errors in 2023 and 2024 revenue, contract balances and remaining performance obligations, and the 2026 quarterly reports describe it as remediated by 2026-06-30. The original 2024 annual report classified the 2027 convertible notes as long-term and the 2025 annual report shows them as current; the carrying amount is the same, so debt and net debt are unaffected, but current liabilities differ.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–148; 10-Q_2026-06-30_axon_axon-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-K_2024-12-31_axon_axon-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85

## Gaps
- High: no source states the legal rank or security of the 2030, 2031 and 2033 notes, so the debt stack is not drawn and note ranking is not established; the action is to obtain the indentures.

- Medium: the debt note prints only a total carrying amount, so the carrying value of each note is not stated and the principal of each note stands in the instrument table beside one financing cost adjustment row.

- Medium: the quarterly reports state compliance with the revolver covenants but print no ratio, and the covenant levels after the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so covenant headroom is not established; the action is to obtain the compliance certificates.

- Medium: reported EBITDA includes other income, net, mostly gains on strategic investments, and adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026 without recasting 2025, so leverage and cover are shown on both measures and neither is clean; the action is to restate the 2025 periods on the 2026 definition.
- Medium: the cash share of the Skydio tender offer and secondary purchases and the date of each closing are not established, so the pro forma net debt for those purchases is not stated.

- Low: cash flow lines that the filings print as a dash are marked Not supplied rather than zero, and lines that a filing does not print at all are marked Not supplied; these cells are in the cash flow table and affect no printed subtotal.
- Low: annual recurring revenue is not stated in the quarterly reports, so the series stops at the 2025 year end; the action is to read the issuer's investor materials.
- Low: the remaining performance obligations of the original 2024 report may carry the immaterial errors the 2025 annual report describes; the value is shown as printed.

- Low: the 2027 convertible notes were classified as long-term in the original 2024 report and as current in the 2025 annual report; the 2025 annual report is used for 2024 balances and the carrying amount is unchanged.
- Low: the segment realignment means segment figures before 2024 are not on the current basis.
- Low: the Q3 2026 report is unaudited and the period from 2026-11-05 to the as-of date is not covered by any supplied document.

# Business & governance: Axon Enterprise, Inc.
## Request

Business and governance work for Axon Enterprise, Inc. (issuer axon-1069183), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business model, ownership and control, transactions and capital allocation, drawn from the five supplied filings and the source readiness result. No peer comparison, instrument view or recovery view is given.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Axon is a listed public-safety technology issuer with no disclosed controlling holder, whose credit rests on recurring public-sector software contracts and a record of buying out stakes it already holds, so creditors depend on management's own financial policy.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; Source readiness (CP-0)

That policy is, on the evidence, cash-funded and free of payouts: no dividends and no program repurchases through 2025, USD 1,820,710 thousand of cash spent on acquisitions from 2024 to the first nine months of 2026, and an equity program that raised USD 489,554 thousand in 2025. The weak points are a governance record with two year-end control failures and a USD 1.2 billion Skydio commitment whose cash call is up to USD 720.0 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 147–148; 10-K_2024-12-31_axon_axon-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 167–168; calculation C11
### Key findings

Recurring software is now the larger and faster-growing half of the business, which gives creditors contracted visibility but ties it to public budgets. Software and Services made up 45.39% of net sales in the nine months of 2026 against 43.38% a year earlier and grew 38.28%, while Connected Devices grew 27.46%. Remaining performance obligations were USD 10.2 billion at 2026-09-30, and Axon expects 20% to 25% of that within 12 months, so most of the contracted value is realised over several years and depends on agency appropriations. Sales are concentrated by geography, with 82.47% in the United States, and the largest customer vertical is law enforcement, although no customer exceeded 10% of net sales in 2025, 2024 or 2023.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6

Ownership and control are only partly established: no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, but the filings give no holder percentages, board independence or related-party detail, because those items sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The 2025 annual report was signed by 8 directors, including the chief executive, against 10 a year earlier; three earlier signatories are absent and one new director appears, and the filings give no reason. The chief executive is also a director, the officer who reviews segment results and the holder of a shareholder-approved equity award, so board oversight of that role matters, and its independence cannot be tested without the proxy.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 149–150; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-K_2024-12-31_axon_axon-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 175–176; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C32

Payout policy is creditor-friendly on the evidence, but equity pay is settled partly in cash. Axon has declared no dividends and says it does not intend to, and it repurchased no shares under its authorised program in 2023, 2024 or 2025, leaving USD 16.3 million of the authorisation unused. Instead, net-settling employee equity awards took cash payments of USD 350,981 thousand in 2025 and USD 167,156 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, equal to 55.34% and 38.42% of stock-based compensation expense, while an at-the-market equity program raised USD 489,554 thousand in 2025 and USD 100,259 thousand in 2026 to date, which adds to equity and not to debt. Shares outstanding rose 6.25% between 2024-12-31 and 2026-09-30.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18

Acquisitions follow a consistent pattern of building a minority stake and then buying the rest with cash, which concentrates integration and goodwill risk. Axon held 20.3%, 20.2%, 0.8% and 10.7% of Fusus, Dedrone, Prepared and Carbyne before buying the remaining interests in January 2024, October 2024, October 2025 and February 2026. Cash paid for business combinations was USD 1,820,710 thousand from 2024 to the first nine months of 2026, and goodwill and intangible assets reached USD 2,154,165 thousand, 24.39% of total assets at 2026-09-30. Remeasuring the stakes it already held produced non-taxable gains of USD 134.1 million across the four deals. This is an inference from four completed cases, and the filings do not say Axon intends to buy the rest of Skydio, in which it holds 15%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 137–139; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C27

The Skydio commitment is the largest transaction still open, and it moves cash out of the company without moving control. On 2026-11-05 Axon agreed to non-voting minority investments of up to USD 1.2 billion that would lift its stake from 15% to about 37% on a fully diluted basis, settled with up to USD 720.0 million of cash and the rest in shares. USD 127.5 million was paid at the primary closing, which leaves up to USD 592.5 million of cash for the tender offer and secondary purchases expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027, equal to 36.12% of cash and short-term investments at 2026-09-30. Axon says it has no significant influence over Skydio, so the stake is accounted for under the measurement alternative and later price changes would pass through earnings without moving cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26

Strategic investments now carry a meaningful share of balance-sheet value and of reported earnings, so creditors cannot rely on them to service debt. Strategic investments were USD 924,934 thousand at 2026-09-30, 2.22x their USD 416,833 thousand at 2025-12-31 and 10.47% of total assets, and other income, net, which is mainly gains on these investments, was 82.01% of income before tax in the nine months of 2026. The filings attribute most of the gain to observable price changes at one investee without naming it, so whether it is Skydio is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13

Creditor protection rests on filing summaries and on a structure with no subsidiary guarantees. The notes and the revolver are the parent's obligations, none of its subsidiaries guarantees the senior or convertible notes, and the non-guarantor subsidiaries produced 19% of nine-month net sales and held 17% of consolidated assets. The revolver is senior unsecured at USD 500.0 million after the September 2026 amendment, undrawn, with letters of credit of USD 9.1 million, and a change of control would oblige Axon to offer to repurchase the senior notes at 101%. The covenant levels after the amendment and every restricted-payment, investment and lien basket are not printed, so what the documents allow cannot be set against what Axon has done.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; Source readiness (CP-0)

The reporting record is the weakest governance evidence, although it is improving. Management reported a material weakness in revenue-recognition controls at both 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31, an amended 2024 annual report restated the classification of the 2027 convertible notes, and earlier statements were revised for principal-versus-agent accounting; the weakness was reported remediated at 2026-06-30 and disclosure controls were effective at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30. The auditor changed in 2024. For creditors the consequence is lower comfort in covenant and leverage figures built from the 2024 and 2025 statements, not a doubt about the current quarter.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_axon_axon-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 167–168; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 144–148; 10-Q_2026-06-30_axon_axon-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52

Operating risk centres on margin mix and government budgets rather than on volume. In the nine months of 2026 gross margin fell to 58.72% from 60.36%, and Connected Devices adjusted gross margin to 49.6% from 52.0%, as Platform Solutions, driven by counter-drone equipment whose timing depends on large contracts, grew 108.57%. Operating income was USD 118,101 thousand, 4.51% of net sales, so debt service depends on sustaining subscription growth and on balance-sheet cash and not yet on operating margin.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is that Axon behaves conservatively where creditors are most exposed: it pays no dividends, funds acquisitions from cash on hand, reports USD 1,640,404 thousand of cash and short-term investments at 2026-09-30 against USD 2,900,000 thousand of notes, and has USD 10.2 billion of contracted obligations behind its software revenue, and its revenue-recognition control weakness has been reported remediated. The view would move toward low governance risk if a proxy statement showed an independent board, no related-party dealings and a dispersed share register, and if the indentures showed tight limits on payments and investments. It would move the other way if the Skydio closings use cash near the USD 720.0 million ceiling and a stake of about 37% is followed by an agreement to take control, if the strategic investment gains reverse, if another control weakness is reported, or if acquisitions start to be funded with debt.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_axon_axon-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C26
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not in the source set, so holder percentages, board independence, committee roles and related-party dealings are not established; the finding that no holder controls Axon rests on the filings naming none, and a disclosed large holder would reverse it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 149–150; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment and lien capacity is not established; the finding that payout policy is creditor-friendly describes behaviour to date and not what the documents permit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–57; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The Skydio terms come from a one-paragraph subsequent-event note, so the final cash and share mix, the closing dates and the investee's own financial position are not established; the cash call could be anywhere up to the stated ceiling, which changes how much of the liquidity finding is already committed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

- The subsidiary list is not in the supplied text, so the legal structure below the four acquired companies is not established; the finding that no subsidiary guarantees the notes cannot be tested against claims at entity level.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153

- The filings do not name the investee behind most of the strategic investment gains, so whether those gains depend on Skydio is not established; the finding on earnings quality could be stronger or weaker once the investee is known.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16
### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Axon has completed four acquisitions since January 2024, each of an entity in which it already held a minority interest, and in September 2026 it raised and re-sized its debt ahead of a further minority investment. Fusus (2024-01-31) and Dedrone (2024-10-01) were followed by Prepared (2025-10-01) and Carbyne (2026-02-18); the Carbyne cash paid was USD 551.7 million net of cash acquired and of equity attributable to pre-combination service, against a base purchase price of USD 625.0 million stated in the 2025 annual report, and Axon funded it from cash on hand.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 137–140; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

Two debt events frame the creditor position. In March 2025 Axon issued USD 1,000,000 thousand of 6.125% senior notes due 2030 and USD 750,000 thousand of 6.250% senior notes due 2033, and in September 2026 it issued USD 1,150,000 thousand of zero-coupon convertible senior notes due 2031 with a conversion price of USD 652.06, buying capped calls for USD 114,885 thousand. The same month it amended the revolver to USD 500.0 million, extending its maturity to the earliest of 2031-09-18 and dates 91 days before the 2031 notes' maturity or holder repurchase date. All 2027 convertible notes were exchanged, redeemed or converted by 2026-02-11.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 116–120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–23

The open transaction is Skydio: agreements signed on 2026-11-05 for non-voting minority investments of up to USD 1.2 billion, with up to USD 720.0 million in cash and the rest in shares, of which USD 127.5 million of cash was paid at the primary closing. Closings of the remaining tender offer and secondary purchases are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027. This is a subsequent event and is not part of any period figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

# Fundamental credit: Axon Enterprise, Inc.
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Axon Enterprise, Inc. (issuer axon-1069183), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: overall credit profile, strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside path, built from the five supplied filings and the three earlier module results. No rating, security view, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Axon is an adequate fundamental credit: liquidity, a multi-year contracted software base and no debt due before 2030 support creditors, but thin free cash flow, investment-dependent earnings and a Skydio cash call mean leverage looks safer than it is.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Net debt was USD 1,409.22 million at 2026-09-30, which is 3.21x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and USD 1,536.72 million or 3.50x pro forma for the USD 127.5 million paid to Skydio on 2026-11-05. Before other income, net debt is 7.49x EBITDA, and the pro forma figure on that measure is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation I1; calculation I2; calculation I3; calculation I4; calculation I5
### Key findings

Liquidity is the strongest support, because it covers debt service and the Skydio cash call without any market access. Cash, short-term investments, marketable securities and the undrawn revolver came to USD 2,146,055 thousand at 2026-09-30, before the Skydio payments, and no note falls due before 2030-03-15. The Skydio cash ceiling of USD 720.0 million is 33.55% of that liquidity, so the buffer survives the commitment, but the pro forma liquidity figure is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C17; calculation C4

Leverage is moderate or high depending on the earnings measure, and the measure that excludes investment gains is the more reliable. Net debt is 3.21x reported EBITDA (3.50x pro forma for the Skydio payment on 2026-11-05) and 1.59x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, whose pro forma figure is not established. Cash interest cover is 4.03x on reported EBITDA and 8.13x on adjusted EBITDA. The revolver tests net leverage at 3.50x and interest cover at 3.50x, but the definitions differ from these ratios and the levels after the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so headroom is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation I3; calculation I4; calculation I6; calculation I7; calculation I8

Free cash flow stability is the weakest dimension, because free cash flow is thin and turns negative once the cash taxes on employee equity awards are counted. Last-twelve-month free cash flow was USD 80,912 thousand after capital spending of USD 144,570 thousand, while cash taxes paid on net-settled awards were USD 308,506 thousand, a shortfall of USD 227,594 thousand. An equity offering program raised USD 227,572 thousand over the same twelve months, so the cash taxes on equity pay were met from new equity, not from internal cash flow.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation I14; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Earnings quality is the second constraint: 57.12% of reported EBITDA is other income, mainly gains on strategic investments that carry no cash. EBITDA before other income was USD 188,261 thousand, and net debt is 7.49x that figure, with the pro forma figure on that measure not established. The mechanism is that a fall in an investee's valuation would lower reported EBITDA and raise reported leverage without any change in operations, so creditors should read leverage from operating earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation I9; calculation I10; calculation I5

Revenue visibility is high, and it is the main reason the credit is not weaker. Remaining performance obligations were USD 10.2 billion at 2026-09-30, of which 20% to 25% is expected within 12 months, and Software and Services grew 38.28% in the nine months of 2026. Renewal rates and customer churn are not stated, and the contracts depend on public appropriations, so the backlog supports revenue timing more than it guarantees cash.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C13

Margins are thin, although operating leverage has turned positive. In the nine months of 2026 gross margin fell to 58.72% from 60.36%, and operating income was 4.51% of net sales, yet operating expenses grew 17.52% against net sales growth of 32.15%. Hardware mix, memory costs and large counter-drone contracts, whose timing is volatile, can reverse that leverage quickly.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C14; calculation C15

Refinancing risk is far away but concentrated. USD 2,150,000 thousand falls due or can be put by holders between 2030-03-15 and 2031-03-20, the 2031 convertible notes may be settled in cash, shares or both, and the revolver maturity can spring forward to 91 days before the notes' maturity or repurchase date. Axon raised USD 1,750,000 thousand of senior notes in 2025 and USD 1,150,000 thousand of convertible notes in 2026, which shows market access, but no rating or market price is supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; calculation C7

Financial policy is creditor-friendly on payouts and acquisitive on investment, and governance evidence is incomplete. Axon pays no dividends and repurchased no shares under its program through 2025, but it spent USD 1,820,710 thousand of cash on acquisitions from 2024 to the first nine months of 2026, reported a revenue-recognition control weakness at both 2024 and 2025 year ends, and has not supplied board independence or holder percentages. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 147–148; calculation C19
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a stronger credit is that Axon holds more liquidity than its leverage ratios suggest, pays no distributions, and is covered 8.13x on issuer-adjusted cash interest with net leverage of 1.59x on that measure (the pro forma figure is not established). On that reading the thin free cash flow is a choice to fund growth and equity pay, and the gains in other income are a bonus and not a support. That view would win if the investment gains proved recurring or realised in cash, if free cash flow after equity-pay taxes turned positive without new equity, and if the executed debt documents showed tight limits on payments and investments. The view would weaken if the Skydio cash settlement approached the USD 720.0 million ceiling while operating cash flow stayed weak, if the investment gains reversed, if the equity offering program were no longer available, or if the share price reached the level at which holders may convert the 2031 notes and Axon chose cash settlement.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation I6; calculation I8
### Limitations

- No rating, market price, spread or peer figure is supplied, so the judgement that Axon is an adequate credit against typical high yield issuers and the finding that market access is a strength rest on the filings alone, and either could change once market levels are known.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The revolver covenants are defined on a different basis from the reported ratios and their levels after the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so the leverage finding cannot be tested against a covenant and headroom could be larger or smaller than the reported ratios imply.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130

- The issuer changed its adjusted EBITDA definition in 2026 without restating 2025, so the 1.59x adjusted leverage (pro forma figure not established) and the 8.13x adjusted cover blend two definitions and could be overstated as a comparison with earlier quarters.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- No management guidance, forecast or earnings release is supplied, so the outlook and the downside scenario are qualitative and the size of a revenue shock that would exhaust liquidity is not established.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The final cash share of the Skydio tender offer and secondary purchases is not known, so leverage after the full commitment is not established and the pro forma finding stops at the primary closing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33
- Counter-drone sales, customer-level revenue and renewal rates are not separated in the filings, so the revenue durability finding cannot be sized by customer or by product beyond the segment lines.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40
### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
### Strengths and weaknesses

The credit has five supports. Liquidity ranks first, because USD 2,146,055 thousand of cash, investments and undrawn revolver stands before the Skydio payments and no debt is due before 2030-03-15, so interest and the cash call are covered without market access. The contracted software base ranks second, because USD 10.2 billion of remaining performance obligations gives revenue visibility that supports interest cover. Payout discipline ranks third, because no dividends or program repurchases keep cash in the company. Market access ranks fourth, because Axon placed USD 1,750,000 thousand of senior notes in 2025 and USD 1,150,000 thousand of convertible notes in 2026. Scale ranks fifth, because last-twelve-month net sales of USD 3,417,012 thousand and a customer base with no customer above 10% of sales absorb ordinary shocks.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8

The credit has five constraints. Free cash flow ranks first, because USD 80,912 thousand of free cash flow is less than the USD 308,506 thousand of equity-award taxes paid in cash and the gap was filled by new equity. Earnings quality ranks second, because other income is 57.12% of reported EBITDA and net debt is 7.49x EBITDA before other income (pro forma figure not established), so reported leverage understates exposure. Skydio and acquisition cash calls rank third, because up to USD 720.0 million of cash goes into a minority stake that Axon does not control. Margin dilution ranks fourth, because gross margin fell to 58.72% and counter-drone mix lowers the Connected Devices margin. The governance and control record ranks fifth, because the proxy statement is missing and a control weakness was open at two year ends.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C2

### Company description

Axon sells integrated public-safety hardware and software, and its credit case rests on how much of that revenue recurs. Software and Services, which is subscription cloud evidence, records and real-time operations software with related services, made up 45.39% of net sales in the nine months of 2026, and Connected Devices (TASER devices, cameras, drones and counter-drone equipment) made up the rest. Customers are public agencies, enterprises and consumers, 82.47% of nine-month sales were in the United States, and no customer exceeded 10% of net sales, so concentration is by budget cycle and not by account.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; calculation C8

The model supports cash-flow visibility, because multi-year contracts produced USD 10.2 billion of remaining performance obligations, and it supports refinancing confidence through scale, but it weakens debt service capacity in the near term, because hardware sales and large counter-drone orders arrive in lumps and subscription billing spreads cash over time. Axon has bought out four companies in which it already held minority stakes since January 2024, so growth has been partly acquired, with goodwill and intangible assets at 24.39% of total assets at 2026-09-30.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 137–139; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Ownership and group structure

Axon is a listed company with no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder, so creditors cannot assume sponsor support or sponsor extraction. Business & governance found no dividends or program repurchases, eight directors who signed the 2025 annual report against ten a year earlier, a chief executive who is also a director and the officer who reviews segment results, and no holder percentages, because the proxy statement is not supplied. Group structure is simple for creditors: the notes and revolver are the parent's obligations, no subsidiary guarantees the notes, and non-guarantor subsidiaries produced 19% of nine-month net sales and held 17% of consolidated assets, so the notes have no direct claim on those entities.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 154

Financial policy so far is creditor-friendly on payouts and moderately aggressive on investment: Axon raised senior and convertible debt, bought capped calls for USD 114,885 thousand to limit dilution, and committed to Skydio, while equity programs funded employee taxes. Governance and sponsor risk is rated Medium by Business & governance, because the control weakness record and the missing proxy statement offset the absence of any extraction.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is mostly recurring or contracted, public-sector and not cyclical in the usual sense, but it is exposed to budgets and to lumpy hardware orders. Software and Services grew 38.28% in the nine months of 2026, driven by more users and adoption of premium add-ons, TASER grew 11.93% on TASER 10 volume, and Platform Solutions grew 108.57% on counter-drone equipment, whose timing depends on large customer contracts. Pricing power is not established: the filings state premium adoption but no price or renewal data.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C16

The risk mechanism is that agencies can fail to appropriate funds or terminate for convenience, so booked backlog converts to cash only as budgets allow; a government funding disruption, such as the 2025 shutdown the filing cites, delays billing and collection. The credit implication is that revenue timing, and not revenue loss, is the main risk, and subscription billing makes receivables and contract assets absorb cash first.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are largely fixed in the short run, which makes margins sensitive to growth. Operating expenses were 54.22% of net sales in the nine months of 2026 against 60.96% a year earlier, selling, general and administrative costs rose with headcount of more than 5,100 full-time employees at 2025-12-31, and stock-based compensation was 16.60% of net sales. Gross margin fell as hardware mix, memory costs and professional services rose, partly offset by USD 47.4 million of tariff refunds.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C6; calculation C18

Margins can be defended against a modest volume shock because research and capital spending are discretionary, but not against an adverse mix or a memory-cost shock, because the annual report warns that raw-material price changes for the TASER 10 device may not be passed through to customers. The credit implication is that EBITDA before other income, of USD 188,261 thousand, is the right margin base for stress, and not reported EBITDA.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital intensity is moderate and flexible, but cash conversion is weak. Last-twelve-month capital spending of USD 144,570 thousand was 4.23% of net sales, working capital consumed USD 448,926 thousand of receivables and contract assets and USD 238,141 thousand of inventory in the nine months of 2026, and free cash flow was USD 80,912 thousand, 18.43% of reported EBITDA and 9.14% of adjusted EBITDA. Free cash flow before cash interest covers cash interest 1.74x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

The mechanism is that growth is financed by working capital and by cash paid for employee equity taxes, so EBITDA overstates cash available for debt service. Capital spending can be cut over the maturity wall, and open purchase orders of about USD 1.2 billion at 2025-12-31 include cancellable orders, although the filing says the ability to cancel is limited by vendor relationships, and the cloud hosting commitment has USD 154.9 million remaining.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation C1; calculation C2
### Porter's Five Forces

Competitive rivalry is high and fragmented: the annual report lists dozens of competitors across body cameras, evidence software, records, real-time operations and counter-drone systems, including Motorola Solutions, so price and feature competition can compress margins. The threat of new entrants is moderate, because agencies require integration with evidence workflows and the TASER 10 device needs a federal firearms license, but the records software area is fragmented with more than 50 providers. The threat of substitutes is moderate, because less-lethal alternatives such as pepper spray and rubber rounds compete with conducted energy devices. Buyer power is meaningful, because buyers are public agencies with open bidding and appropriation cycles, though none exceeds 10% of sales. Supplier power is moderate to high for the TASER 10 device, because a limited number of suppliers provide its raw materials and Axon states it cannot change suppliers easily, and memory costs rose.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

The credit translation is that rivalry and buyer power cap pricing, supplier power exposes hardware margins, and entry barriers protect the software base, which is why Connected Devices carries the margin risk and Software and Services the stability.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### PEST

Political and regulatory factors are material, and economic factors are partly material. Public budgets and appropriations drive demand, the TASER 10 device is classified as a firearm and needs a federal firearms license, exports need licences, privacy and artificial intelligence laws apply, and tariffs and their refund after the Supreme Court decision of 2026-02-20 moved gross margin. Social and technological factors matter to demand and competition but not directly to debt service.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### SWOT

Strengths: the contracted software base, liquidity, no sponsor extraction and market access support credit. Weaknesses: thin free cash flow after equity-pay taxes, reliance on investment gains in reported EBITDA, and a record of control weaknesses constrain it. Opportunities: faster software growth, which carries a 75.3% adjusted gross margin against 49.6% in Connected Devices, could lift margins and cash conversion. Threats: public budget shocks, counter-drone volatility and a reversal of investment gains could weaken credit quality.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is strong: last-twelve-month net sales of USD 3,417,012 thousand and a US law-enforcement base, though market share is not supplied. Competitive advantage is average: integrated hardware and cloud contracts suggest switching costs, but retention is not stated and competition is broad. Business diversification is average: four product lines and no customer above 10% of sales, against 82.47% of sales in one country and one buyer type. Cost and capex flexibility is average. Margin stability is average: stable on issuer-adjusted measures but thin and volatile on reported operating margin. Free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow is USD 80,912 thousand and negative after equity-award taxes. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is strong, on demonstrated issuance and equity depth, though no rating or price is supplied. Liquidity position is strong. Financial policy and governance is average, with Medium governance risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_axon_axon-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C2

The main supports are liquidity, contracted revenue and payout discipline; the constraints are free cash flow and earnings quality; the trend in net leverage on reported EBITDA is down, from 5.14x at 2026-03-31 to 3.21x at 2026-09-30 (3.50x pro forma for the payment of 2026-11-05), but it rests on investment gains. The missing datapoints are covenant headroom, ratings, guidance and holder percentages.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation I3; calculation I4; calculation I18
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months, tailwinds are backlog conversion (the 20% to 25% expected within 12 months), software adoption and positive operating leverage, and headwinds are the Skydio cash settlement, memory costs, counter-drone timing and tariffs. The effect is to support revenue and interest cover while pressuring liquidity and free cash flow after equity-award taxes. Over three to five years, the 2030 senior notes and the 2031 convertible notes come due or can be put within 12 months of each other, so deleveraging depends on cash flow improving or on equity funding continuing; the sector tailwind is demand for public-safety technology, and the headwind is budget dependence and competition.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C7
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a public-budget or appropriation delay that coincides with a fall in large counter-drone orders and further memory-cost pressure. The first operational break is slower Connected Devices shipments, which carry the lower margin (49.6% adjusted gross margin) and which already fell from 52.0%. Financial transmission follows through gross margin and operating income, which was only 4.51% of net sales, and through working capital, because receivables and inventory absorb cash before it returns. If investment gains reverse, reported EBITDA falls toward EBITDA before other income of USD 188,261 thousand and net debt reaches 7.49x that figure, and the pro forma figure on that measure is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14; calculation I5

Liquidity and refinancing consequences are bounded by USD 2,146,055 thousand of liquidity before Skydio, the up to USD 720.0 million Skydio cash ceiling and the absence of maturities before 2030-03-15. Management levers are cutting capital spending and research spending and choosing share settlement of the 2031 notes, and, because equity awards vest on share-price goals, a fall in the share price would also reduce the cash taxes paid on net settlement. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress for several years, but not sufficient to keep reported net leverage near 3.21x (3.50x pro forma for the payment of 2026-11-05) if the investment gains reverse. The observable triggers are listed in the monitoring register, and the primary downside path is a reversal of investment gains and a stall in free cash flow while Skydio cash leaves and the 2030 to 2031 maturities approach.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_axon_axon-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C17; calculation C4; calculation C7
### Overall credit view

Overall, Axon presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring software contracts, large liquidity and payout discipline, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow after equity-award taxes, investment-dependent earnings and growing acquisition and investment cash calls. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate, because EBITDA converts poorly to free cash flow and the equity programs fill the gap. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access and liquidity in 2029 and 2030, because USD 2,150,000 thousand falls due or can be put within 12 months. The primary downside path is a reversal of investment gains with stalled free cash flow, and further analysis would require ratings, covenant levels after the amendment, guidance, the proxy statement and the executed debt documents.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C2
Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: reported leverage depends on investment gains while free cash flow after equity-award taxes is negative.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2
